evidence.field: 形義通解；甲骨文及金文用例
evidence.text: The entry reports several early analyses. One oracle-bone form joins 日 and 月; Xu Zhongshu interprets it as dawn, while Shen Pei proposes brightness. Another uses 月 with 囧, described as a lattice window and also a sound element, interpreted as moonlight entering through a window. The entry says 目+月 examples are too fragmentary to identify securely, and 田+月 may reflect corruption of 日 or 囧. It cites oracle-bone examples for dawn (合集481) and brightness (合集21037), and bronze examples for dawn and later senses including clear, manifest, and morally upright. These are the database’s reported readings; I did not inspect the underlying inscription images.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 明

evidence.text: The entry quotes 說文: 朙 means ‘illuminate’ and is formed from 月 and 囧; 明 is identified there as an ancient form of 朙. The database’s separate 囧 analysis describes the graph as a lattice window, while quoting 說文’s ‘read like 明’ report. This historical phonetic note does not by itself establish the original spoken name of the depicted object or resolve the proposed phonetic relation.

evidence.text: The record groups 明 forms under oracle bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small seal, and Shuowen ancient-script headings. It explains 明 as 日 plus 月 for brightness and identifies bronze example 集成00161. This is one account of the forms, not evidence that it is the sole early analysis.

evidence.text: The file description identifies this as a digital vector image of 明 in Shang oracle-script style and cites source collections including Sinica and CUHK; it also points to a specific Hanziyuan image. Commons labels the representation public domain, including release of any copyright generated in making the file. It is a modern vector rendering, not an artifact photograph. The inspected description page’s original-file link resolves to https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4a/%E6%98%8E-oracle.svg, but fetching that image returned HTTP 429 during this session.

gaps: The relative chronology of early meanings remains unsettled: the CUHK entry reports both dawn and brightness in oracle-bone examples, and the form record does not establish which sense came first.

The phonetic analysis of 囧 in the 月+囧 form is reported by CUHK but is not independently demonstrated by the inspected material. The original object’s spoken name is not established; the window depiction alone cannot establish a historical sound match.
The oracle-bone and bronze examples are reported by the dictionary; their underlying inscription images were not inspected, and individual artifact dates were not established in this research pass.
Official Unihan character-specific records for 明 and 囧 could not be opened. Current Mandarin readings are therefore not externally verified here.

The exact Commons image candidate is documented and its direct URL was recovered, but the image request returned HTTP 429. No glyph candidate is selected because its pixels were not available for this sourcing pass; no alternate image with sufficiently verified provenance and reuse rights was established. The Commons file is explicitly a modern vector rendering, not an ancient artifact photograph.

limitations.text: A candidate for a Shang oracle-style modern vector rendering was identified on its exact Commons description page. Its original image URL returned HTTP 429, so it is not proposed as a selected asset; the page records public-domain status and a stated source lineage.
